reference_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per activation event
  SELECT user_id, event_name,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts DESC, event_name) AS rn
  FROM activation_events
)
SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) AS users
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY event_name
alternatives:
WITH latest AS (  -- one row per activated user
  SELECT ae.user_id, ae.event_name
  FROM activation_events ae
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM activation_events ae2
                    WHERE ae2.user_id = ae.user_id
                      AND (ae2.event_ts > ae.event_ts OR (ae2.event_ts = ae.event_ts AND ae2.event_name < ae.event_name)))
)
SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) AS users
FROM latest
GROUP BY event_name

SELECT t.event_name, COUNT(*) AS users
FROM (
  -- one row per activation event, numbered within its user from the latest
  SELECT user_id, event_name,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts DESC, event_name) AS rn
  FROM activation_events
) AS t
WHERE t.rn = 1
GROUP BY t.event_name

other_way.sql:
WITH latest AS (  -- one row per activated user
  SELECT ae.user_id, ae.event_name
  FROM activation_events ae
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM activation_events ae2
                    WHERE ae2.user_id = ae.user_id
                      AND (ae2.event_ts > ae.event_ts OR (ae2.event_ts = ae.event_ts AND ae2.event_name < ae.event_name)))
)
SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) AS users
FROM latest
GROUP BY event_name
other_way.tradeoff: NOT EXISTS finds each user's latest event without a window, but the self-comparison is slower on a big table.
